why: Both moved the same single routable call site (the OpenAI planner) with the same dated-snapshot model_map and the same honest 'stays' reasoning, so the migration is a near tie — the decision is the system-level work on top. B's is deeper and measured end-to-end (18x-understated cost display fixed from usage.cost, the counterintuitive finding that gpt-4o-mini costs more than gpt-4o on screenshots because of 33x image tokenization, a reproduced json.loads crash fixed with provider-enforced schema, a dispatch bug that made advertised planner models raise on selection, a priced 20x model spread, and computer-use tool types actually probed against Router), whereas A ships two items and gets the prompt-caching analysis wrong.
A_best: Found the image/jpeg-on-PNG bug independently and paired it with the one win B missed entirely — reusing the OpenAI client per key instead of rebuilding it (plus a test), a real per-step latency saving on an interactive call; also the cleanest migration detail: an explicit feature='planner' label that the policy and Router spend both key on, rather than B's auto file:function glob.
B_best: The cost work: reading Router's usage.cost showed the on-screen spend estimate was 18.1x low, and pricing the planner's real workload across six catalog models exposed that the app's 'cheap' option (gpt-4o-mini) is both dearer and slower than gpt-4o for screenshots — an expert, non-obvious, measured finding that reframes what to change about this app.
A_worst: The note rejecting prompt caching is wrong for this app: it treats the system prompt as the only stable prefix, when loop.py appends history with the screenshot last, so each turn re-sends a large stable prefix — B measured 2,048 cached tokens and -40% on turn two. A also missed that gpt-4o-mini and the ssh Qwen option crash on selection in the UI while citing gpt-4o-mini as a live planner model, and shipped a cross-vendor fallback whose rescue behaviour it admits was never measured.
B_worst: The report is truncated mid-item (i6) and leaves eight improvements merely proposed, and its live traffic includes unlabelled bench/probe requests and six errors; the migration also keys policy on a function-path glob and leaves the verbose file:function string as the Router spend label, which is weaker attribution than A's explicit 'planner' feature.
